reconcile.note: Henry distinguishes lying wonders that prop up false doctrine from true miracles that seal already-revealed truth, so only Christ's signs certify a genuine divine commission.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza notes Moses commands death for a prophet who preaches new gods even while working real signs and wonders, since God tests His people through such wonders.

quotes.text: Moses lays down the punishment of death for the prophet who preaches new gods, even though he confirm his doctrine by signs and wonders (Deut. xiii.); "For," he says, "the Lord also worketh signs and wonders to try His people."
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part I, ch. II, "Of Prophets" (1670, trans. Elwes 1883), on Deuteronomy 13.

sides.snippet: you shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of dreams
sides.verseText: you shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of dreams: for Yahweh your God proves you, to know whether you love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

sides.snippet: for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.
sides.verseText: The same came to him by night, and said to him, \"Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.\"
